claims: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft reaches over 24,500 mph (approx. 39,400 kph) during translunar injection.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft reaches up to 25,000 mph (40,000 kph) during Earth re-entry.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft slowed to roughly 1,000–3,000 mph relative to the Moon during its lunar flyby.
As of April 2026, the Artemis II mission's Translunar Injection (Leaving Earth) speed is approximately 24,527 mph (39,472 kph) to escape Earth’s gravity.
As of April 2026, the Artemis II mission's Lunar Flyby (Closest Approach) speed is approximately 3,139 mph (5,052 kph) relative to the Moon.
As of April 2026, the Artemis II mission's Re-entry speed is around 25,000 mph (40,000 kph).
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft uses the atmosphere to slow down for splashdown during re-entry
